title: The universal surjective-flat locus in the base is open
statement: Let $B,A,C$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:A\to B$ and $q:C\to B$ be morphisms, and let $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Assume $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and a closed map of underlying topological spaces. Assume $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and a closed map of underlying topological spaces. There is an open subscheme $V\subseteq B$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that for every scheme $T$ and morphism $h:T\to B$, the base change $f_T:A\times_BT\to C\times_BT$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] if and only if $h$ factors through $V\hookrightarrow B$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-relative-universal-flat-open] to $p,q,f$; all its hypotheses are among ours. Obtain the open $F\subseteq B$ and, for every $h:T\to B$, the equivalence between flatness of $f_T$ and factorization of $h$ through $F$. Write $A_F=p^{-1}(F)$ and $C_F=q^{-1}(F)$ with their restricted structure sheaves [def-weil-open-immersion]. Taking $T=F$ and $h$ its inclusion shows that $f_F:A_F\to C_F$ is flat.

Restrict to $F$, writing $A_F=p^{-1}(F)$, $C_F=q^{-1}(F)$ and $f_F:A_F\to C_F$. The restriction is flat by Step 1. It is locally of finite presentation: on compatible affine neighbourhoods over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq F$, write the target as $\operatorname{Spec}D$ and the source as $\operatorname{Spec}E$. The affine-local finite-type and finite-presentation conditions [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] give $D$ finite type over $R$ and $E$ finitely presented over $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra] to $R\to D\to E$ to get finite presentation over $D$. These neighbourhoods cover $A_F$, proving the claim. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open] implies that $I=f_F(|A_F|)$ is open in $|C_F|$.

source.place: Tag 05XC, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-surjective-flat, proof; the flat-case reduction is expanded using Tag 05XB.

proof.text: The map $q_F:C_F\to F$ is closed: a closed subset of $C_F$ is $D\cap q^{-1}(F)$ for a closed $D\subseteq C$, and its image is $q(D)\cap F$, closed in $F$. Apply [lem-sfb-open-image-universal-surjectivity] to $A_F\to C_F\to F$ and the open image $I$ from Step 2. Obtain the open subscheme $V=F\setminus q_F(|C_F|\setminus I)$ of $F$, hence of $B$ [def-weil-open-immersion], representing surjectivity of all base changes over $F$.

For $h:T\to B$ factoring as $\iota_F h\prime$, the fibre products over $B$ identify canonically with $A_F\times_FT$ and $C_F\times_FT$, compatibly with the induced maps [def-pc-fibre-product]. Indeed a compatible test pair into $A$ (respectively $C$) and $T$ lands in the inverse image of $F$ and factors uniquely through that open; compatibility over $F$ is equivalent to compatibility over $B$ because the inclusion of $F$ is injective on maps [def-weil-open-immersion]. If $h$ factors through $V$, Step 1 gives flatness and Step 3 gives surjectivity of $f_T$. Conversely if $f_T$ is flat and surjective, Step 1 factors $h$ through $F$; then Step 3 factors $h\prime$ through $V$. These factorizations compose to the required one over $B$.
